stipend_closure.what: The last runner assumption of BNB is gone: Withdraw.KeepsInv is now PROVED for EthLib's real runner (processRunner / processMessage) for ANY code of the owner, by reuse of TokenKit.Stipend.processMessage_quiet (the theorem WETH uses). No library lemma was missing: no Stipend2.lean, no edit under TokenKit/.
stipend_closure.call_gas: The CALL at pc 3010 asks for gas 2300 * (amount == 0) (Withdraw.askedWord, read from the bytes by the generated path withdrawEther_p2): 0 asked + 2300 stipend when amount != 0, 2300 asked + no stipend when amount = 0. So the message has at most 2300 gas (last field of Withdraw.Payout, proved in withdrawEther_run from callGas_subCall_le and askedWord_le).

theorems.Withdraw.payout_keeps_storage: the message of Payout, run by processRunner with no error, keeps every storage word of the contract. Hypotheses: .istanbul <= fork; the contract account holds code.
theorems.Withdraw.processRunner_keepsInv_any: KeepsInv (processRunner fork bound) message S for every bound, message, state. Hypotheses: .istanbul <= fork; (S.getAccount message.currentTarget).codeHash != EMPTY_CODE_HASH. Nothing on the owner (any code, precompile, delegation).
theorems.Withdraw.supply_withdrawEther_process: supply_withdrawEther under processRunner with no KeepsInv. Hypotheses: .berlin <= fork < .glamsterdam, data size < 2^256, selector, hdel, contract holds code, Inv at start.
theorems.process_step_all_process: process_step_all with no KeepsInv: hw is now only (fork < .glamsterdam and hdel).
theorems.process_step_inv_all_process: process_step_inv_all with no KeepsInv: Inv at the start of any top-level message of CODE gives Inv at its end.

hypotheses_left_process_step_inv_all_pro: K: selector != 0x3bed33ce -> Sep (callKeys message) (keccak separation, assumed)
hw: selector = 0x3bed33ce -> fork < .glamsterdam and hdel (from Prague (.pectra <= fork) the code of the owner is no EIP-7702 delegation)
hproc: processMessage fork message state substate = .ok ended; hI: Inv at the start

why_each_condition.istanbul: hypothesis of processMessage_quiet: SSTORE fails with 2300 gas or less from Istanbul (EIP-2200). No upper fork bound for KeepsInv itself. Implied by Paris / Berlin in the other theorems.
why_each_condition.contract_has_code: the message moves its value out of the contract; EthLib's moveEther may delete an account left empty, an account with code is never empty (moveEther_keeps_storage). Same as hcode of process_step.
why_each_condition.hdel_still_needed: yes, but only for the CALL step of the contract itself: TokenKit.call_outcome (used by withdrawEther_run) does not cover a CALL to a delegated account. It is NOT needed for KeepsInv; before Prague it asks nothing. Same limit as WETH's WithdrawReady.
why_each_condition.before_glamsterdam: call_outcome is proved for the one-counter gas rules before Glamsterdam. Not needed for KeepsInv.

stipend_closure.kept_unchanged: Withdraw.lean, Seq.lean, Sanity/Withdraw.lean and every old theorem (process_step_all, process_step_inv_all, processRunner_keepsInv, ...) are byte-identical; nothing weakened. statement_preservation_method.how: On the box, for the original project and for the migrated one, a Lean command walks every theorem named in Test/Axioms.lean and every definition, structure and constructor of the project or of the generic files that its statement uses (through types and bodies of definitions, not proofs). For each it writes the name with the root namespace removed, a hash of the type and of the body computed after the same removal inside, the list of constants used, and the printed type (pp.fullNames). The two dumps are compared by name; texts are compared with runs of blanks made one blank, because the printer breaks lines by width and names changed length.

statement_preservation_method.result: QNT and WETH: no change. SHIB and BNB: one changed definition (Ro gained the field accounts), which makes ro_name and ro_symbol stronger; for SHIB the library lemma Supply.inv_of_ro takes the stronger Ro as hypothesis. See tokens.<t>.statement_preservation.

how_to_run_for_a_new_token: 1. Make tokens/<t>/ with config/<t>.json (copy the closest of the four: shib = plain ERC20 solc 0.5, qnt = solc 0.4 with mint and a generated dispatcher, bnb = two balance mappings and a value CALL, weth = ether backed with a payable fallback) and data/<t>.runtime.hex. Set root (for example FooVerify), dir (Foo), the functions, slots and selectors.
2. Copy lakefile.lean, lake-manifest.json and lean-toolchain from tokens/shib and change the two names ShibVerify to <Root>. Add <Root>.lean with the imports of the files to build.
3. In tokens/<t>: bash ../../scripts/regen.sh config/<t>.json. With dispatch.generate the dispatcher files are written too. The last step (kit_opens.py) sets the `open TokenKit ...` lines.

4. Write the token-specific files by hand: Sep.lean, Seq.lean, a Sanity/Moves.lean witness, and any function that calls out (patterns: tokens/bnb Withdraw.lean, tokens/weth Withdraw.lean and Invariant.lean). Import generic files as TokenKit.Evm.<File>; run python3 ../../scripts/kit_opens.py . after adding a file.

5. Build on the box: bash scripts/build_box.sh <t> (copies the kit to /home/user/token-kit, builds the library and the token detached, prints the final line and the result of check_axioms.sh). The box needs a built /home/user/usdt-verify next to the kit; nothing of EthLib or Mathlib is fetched or built.

1.what: The hypothesis `hrunner` (over every message of the runner, false for EthLib's processRunner) is gone. withdrawEther now rests on a local assumption in upstream's style: Withdraw.KeepsInv runChild message S := KeepsOn runChild (Payout message S) (InvKept message.currentTarget). It is only about the one message the CALL of withdrawEther sends (code address = the owner in slot 4, value = the amount, sender = the contract, gas = what the CALL forwards), from a caller state that reads as the start state (accounts, storage, code), and only when the runner ends that message with no error.
theorems_retired: Withdraw.withdrawEther_run in its old form (hypothesis hrunner): replaced by the restated theorem of the same name, no hrunner
Withdraw.supply_withdrawEther in its old form (hypothesis hrunner): replaced by the restated theorem of the same name, hypothesis hkeeps : KeepsInv runChild message state
No theorem of the kit takes hrunner any more (grep: only one retirement note in the header of Bnb/Withdraw.lean).
hypotheses_now_assumed: hkeeps : Withdraw.KeepsInv runChild message state (local, one message). PROVED for processRunner when the owner has no code or the code STOP and is no precompile, and the contract account holds code (processRunner_keepsInv, keepsInv_noCode, keepsInv_stop). Still an assumption for an owner with any other code.
hdel : the code of the owner is no EIP-7702 delegation (asked from Pectra only; proved for a plain owner: hdel_of_plain)
hglam : fork < Glamsterdam for withdrawEther (the fork range of EthLib's rules of CALL used here)
hfork : Berlin <= fork (Paris for the whole-message theorems); call data below 2^256 bytes
No keccak hypothesis for withdrawEther (it writes no mapping); Sep (callKeys message) stays assumed for the other selectors, as before.
1.satisfiable_for_real_runner: Machine-checked: Withdraw.processRunner_keepsInv proves KeepsInv for processRunner at every bound for (a) an owner with no code and (b) an owner whose code is the one byte STOP. Withdraw.withdrawEther_pays_closed is a full run with processRunner and amount 1 with no hypothesis but Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam: it ends with no error, the owner has 1 wei more, the contract 1 wei less.
1.sequence_theorems: withdrawEther is back: Calls has the constructor `withdraw` (GoodWithdraw), inv_calls covers it, process_step_withdraw / process_step_all / process_step_inv_all lift it to processMessage under hdel and KeepsInv for processRunner; process_step_inv_plain has no runner assumption at all for a plain owner.
1.amount_0_and_failure_cases: Covered by generality, not by a separate witness: withdrawEther_run and supply_withdrawEther hold for every amount word (amount 0 included: the CALL then moves no value and KeepsInv is asked for that message) and for every run that ends with no error. A run that ends with an error (not the owner, nonzero value sent, contract too poor, call depth 1024, callee fails so the code reverts, out of gas) is rolled back by the message layer: untouched_process_failed, used in process_step_withdraw. NOT done: a separate closed full-run witness with amount 0; an owner with code other than STOP stays under the assumption.
